description: The waybill card's key, assigned once and never reused: a retired card leaves a gap (36). generate_waybill_cards.py renumbers the cards from 1 when it runs, so it is not run against this file until the owner decides (docs/data/sidecars.md).
The industry the card is for (ADR-039). Empty on interchange traffic, which belongs to no industry.
industry for a card to or from an island industry; interchange for a car going straight between Scully Yard and Demmler Yard (the orange and blue waybills to CSX and POHC).

The name across the top of the card: the industry's name with the old spellings A Stucki Co and Ferrel Gas, or INTERCHANGE. Kept because external/sts-helpers reads it; www/scripts/tests/test_industry_ids.py checks it against the id through its alias list.
loaded, inbound_empty (an empty to a load spot), outbound_empty (a generic empty home) or interchange (a through car).
The spot usage the card goes to, as spot_assignments.csv names it. Empty on outbound empties and interchange cards.
The industry's spot numbers the card serves: one (6), a range (1-3) or two ranges. — on interchange cards, empty on outbound empties.
IN to the island or OUT. Empty on interchange cards.

The group the lower table of the card prints for a load named in detail. On an industry card the generator writes it from the usage's load in waybill_loads.csv; on an interchange card this cell is the fact, and the generator reads it.
The car type. Empty on outbound empties, which take any car.
The shipper, for an inbound load or an interchange card.
The receiver, or the yard an outbound empty returns to.
The connection the car moves over.

On interchange traffic: IN or OUT, the side of the deck's loaded routing balance the card counts on (generate_waybill_cards.py counts it with the card's via). Empty on industry traffic. The card does not print it.
